title: Capacity Orchestration & Tenant Safeguards PRD: controlled burst orchestration and visibility
creator: Alyssa Chen
overview: This PRD defines a tenant-focused capacity orchestration and safeguards feature set for Redwood Dedicated customers. The goal is to allow operators to configure controlled burst behavior, visibility into per-tenant reservation usage, and automated admission/fallback policies that preserve SLAs for reserved workloads while enabling efficient utilization of idle capacity.
background: Customers have asked for clearer guarantees and predictable behavior when their reserved capacity is exhausted or when transient traffic spikes occur. Current Dedicated behavior is opaque: tenants either get preempted or degrade unpredictably. This causes customer support escalations and churn. We have many existing initiatives (reservation hedging, soft reserves) but no single UX/API surface that ties policy, telemetry, and enforcement into a coherent product for tenants and platform operators.
goals: Provide tenant-visible dashboards showing reserved pool consumption, burst credit balance, and historical burst usage
Expose simple controls for administrators to set soft-burst budgets, hard caps, and decay rules per reservation
Implement an admission controller that enforces burst budgets and routes overflow to defined fallbacks (lower-tier model variant, queued execution, or reject) with deterministic behavior
Preserve latency SLOs for reserved traffic (P95 < configured target) by prioritizing reserved requests over best-effort when near capacity
Deliver a clear policy-API and Console flow so tenants and platform operators can reason about cost and isolation trade-offs
non_goals: Full multi-region cross-account migration or federation of reservations (out of scope for this iteration)
Large-scale re-architecture of kernel scheduling; we will rely on existing runtime hooks for admission
Automated price changes or billing engine redesign (billing will surface metrics but not change billing behavior in this phase)
user_personas: Platform Engineer configuring reserved capacity and SLAs for an internal product team
SRE responding to overload incidents and needing deterministic tenant behavior
Product/Dev team that wants predictable latency for critical routes and occasional bursts for unpredictable traffic
user_stories: As a Platform Engineer, I want to set a soft-burst budget of 2x for a reserved tenant with a daily decay policy so the tenant can handle brief spikes without impacting others
As an SRE, I want to see a timeline of burst consumption and the reason a request was rejected (evicted due to hard cap, fallback triggered) so I can troubleshoot
As a Developer, I want the console to show what fallback model or route will be used when my reservation saturates so I can test quality trade-offs
requirements: Policy model: support soft_burst_budget (multiplier or token bucket), hard_cap (strict token limit), decay_strategy (linear_decay, exponential_decay), and fallback_policy (model_variant, queued, reject)

Console UI: reserved-pool detail page must show current allocation, live utilization, burst credit balance, 90/95/99th percentiles of latency for reserved vs best-effort, and a timeline of recent evictions/fallbacks
API: CRUD for per-reservation policy objects with validation and audit log entries; endpoints must return deterministic simulated outcome for a given request (dry-run API)
Admission controller: enforces policy at request arrival, atomically decrementing burst tokens and applying fallback routing; must be horizontally scalable and idempotent
Telemetry: emit structured events for every admission decision with fields: reservation_id, tenant_id, decision, reason_code, token_delta, backpressure_score, timestamp
SLO protection: when a reservation is within 5% of configured capacity, reserved requests must be prioritized in scheduling to keep P95 latency at or below configured SLO in >= 99% of 1-hour windows
Integration: hooks for autoscaling to pre-warm nodes based on projected burst consumption; autoscaler must be able to consume burst budget forecasts produced by the policy engine
Migration: default policies for existing reservations must be safe (soft_burst_budget=1.0, hard_cap=reservation_size) unless operator opt-in
Docs & Runbook: release must include admin runbook for common troubleshooting flows and a short FAQ for tenants
acceptance_criteria: Policy CRUD: create/update/delete policy via API and Console; changes appear in audit log within 5s

Admission tests: simulated and e2e tests show that with soft_burst_budget=2.0 and decay_strategy=linear, a tenant can exceed reservation by up to 2x for short bursts and tokens decay according to policy
Fallback behavior: when hard_cap is exceeded, requests are routed to configured fallback; logs show fallback_reason matched to policy
SLO tests: under a synthetic load profile that saturates reservation to 95% sustained with brief spikes, reserved route P95 remains <= configured SLO in 99% of hourly windows
Observability: Console shows live utilization and burst balance, telemetry events contain all required fields and can be queried in monitoring dashboards
Security: policy management endpoints require admin RBAC; unit tests cover authorization checks
Performance: admission controller adds <2ms median overhead to request path under normal load and <10ms 99th latency under high concurrency
Backward compatibility: existing reservations without policies operate with default safe policies and show a migration notice in Console
success_metrics: Reduction in Reserved-capacity support tickets related to unpredictable evictions by 60% within two months of GA
Percentage of dedicated customers using soft-burst configuration >= 30% within first quarter
Mean time to diagnose eviction cause reduced from current baseline by 40% (measured via support ticket resolution time)
No regression in overall Dedicated capacity 99th latency SLO across customers
edge_cases_and_assumptions: Assume runtime exposes atomic reservation token decrement primitives; if not available we'll implement a lightweight centralized admission cache
Edge case: network partition with admission controller shard — fallback to conservative reject decisions to protect reserved SLOs
Assume billing changes are not required to show burst usage; we will surface usage metrics but not alter invoices in this scope
Hot-tenant scenario: a tenant with sustained >3x burst will be subject to operator alerting and manual remediation per runbook
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal dogfood on a subset of Dedicated clusters with Platform teams opt-in for experimentation (2 weeks). Phase 2: Beta with selected customers, feature-flagged per-project and enabled via Console (4 weeks). Phase 3: GA with migration notice, default safe policy for existing reservations, and public docs (2 weeks). Post-GA: iterate on autoscaler integration and advanced fairness knobs.
monitoring_and_alerting: Critical alerts for >3% of reserved requests being evicted in a 5 minute window
Alert when admission controller error rate >0.5%
Dashboard: per-reservation utilization, burst balance, fallback rate, P95 latency split reserved vs fallback
dependencies: Runtime: atomic token operations and admission hook (ENG-22110)
Console: new reserved-pool detail page and policy editor (DES-14072)
Telemetry: schema extension for admission events (ENG-23345)
Autoscaler: ability to accept prewarm hints from policy engine (ENG-23901)
Auth: admin RBAC checks for policy endpoints (ENG-21002)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: admission controller performance regression could increase end-to-end latency; Mitigation: keep admission path minimal and benchmark at scale, provide feature flag to disable enforcement and fall back to legacy behavior
Risk: tenants misconfigure overly permissive soft_burst_budget and incur higher costs; Mitigation: expose cost estimate in Console for configured budget and warn on high forecasted spend
Risk: policy bugs could cause asymmetric fairness across tenants; Mitigation: include canary rollout, circuit breaker, and telemetry-based anomaly detection
Risk: insufficient observability for operators; Mitigation: ship dashboards and an exportable CSV for audit within GA
qa_plan: Unit tests for policy validation and authorization, integration tests for admission controller in staging clusters, chaos tests for shard partitions, e2e SLO tests using synthetic loads. Beta customers to validate real-world workload behavior before GA.
documentation: Admin runbook, Console help text inline in reserved-pool page, API reference for policy endpoints, migration FAQ for existing reservations
open_questions: Should cost be automatically throttled when burst budget is exhausted, or always rely on explicit fallback policy?
What is the default decay_strategy that balances simplicity with effectiveness for most customers?
Do we want an optional tenant-visible SLA badge in Console for reservations that meet stricter isolation controls?
